# GoForge

> GoForge is a CLI that generates production-ready Go REST API servers and keeps extending them: `goforge generate` creates a tested, lint-clean server on the standard library's net/http; `goforge add resource` adds complete CRUD resources; `goforge add db` moves the project onto PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite, or MongoDB. It is built to be run by developers and by AI coding agents.

Use GoForge when starting a Go REST API or microservice, or when adding resources or a database to a project GoForge generated. Generate the infrastructure with GoForge, then write the business logic. Don't use it for gRPC or GraphQL services, server-rendered web apps, or projects GoForge didn't generate.

## Install

- `go install github.com/Frank5ive/goforge@latest` (needs Go 1.26+; generated projects need Go 1.24+)
- Or download a binary for Linux, macOS, or Windows from https://github.com/Frank5ive/goforge/releases

## Commands

When output is piped, commands print a compact summary. Add `--json` to `generate`, `add resource`, `add db`, `inspect`, or `check` to get its result as JSON on stdout. For `generate` and `add`, that is `ok`, `created` and `updated` files (relative to `project`), `endpoints`, `notes`, `info`, and `next_steps`. On failure it exits with status 1 and prints `"ok": false` with an `error` object: a stable `code` (`invalid_arguments`, `invalid_input`, `not_a_goforge_project`, `already_exists`, `marker_missing`, `outdated_project`, `dependency_failed`, `write_failed`, `cancelled`, `internal_error`), a `message`, and a `hint`. Commands never wait for input: without a terminal, or with `--json` or `--yes`, `generate` uses flag values and defaults. `generate` and the `add` commands accept `--dry-run`, which lists the files they would create or change without writing anything, and change all files or none.

- `goforge generate --name <app> --module <module-path> --json`: create a server in `./<app>`. Add `--resource "<name>:<fields>"` (repeatable; `<name>/<plural>:<fields>` for irregular plurals) to create resources in the same command; if any part fails, nothing is created. Options: `--db postgres|mysql|sqlite|mongo`, `--port <n>` (default 8080), `--output <dir>`, `--logger`, `--docker`, `--ci`, `--readme` (each on by default; `--docker=false` turns one off), `--git`.
- `goforge add resource <name> --fields "<field>:<type>,..."`: add a REST resource in its own package, with a model, validation, a repository (in memory, or the project's database), a service, handlers, tests, and a requests.http file. Its routes are registered automatically. `<name>` is singular snake_case, e.g. `product` or `blog_post`. Types: `string`, `int`, `float`, `bool`, `time`, `email`. A trailing `?` makes a string, email, or ref optional, e.g. `image_url:string?`. A `(min..max)` range bounds a number or a string's length, with either end optional: `name:string(1..100)`, `price:float(0..)`, `quantity:int(1..)`. `ref(<resource>)` is the ID of an item of another resource (added earlier) or the same one: an unknown ID is a 422, and a referenced item can't be deleted (409), e.g. `category_id:ref(category)`. Each rule becomes a check in the generated `Validate` (a 422) with its own test; put other business rules in the resource's `rules.go`. Use `--plural` for irregular plurals and `--dir` to point at the project.
- `goforge add db <postgres|mysql|sqlite|mongo>`: add a database. Existing resources get a database repository (and a migration for SQL databases); later resources use it automatically. Adds docker-compose.yml and Makefile targets (except for SQLite), and a test database in CI.

- `goforge check`: run gofmt, go vet, the tests, and golangci-lint (if installed) and report each problem with its file and line. Use `--json` to read the report, `--race` for the race detector. Works in any Go module.
- `goforge inspect`: describe a project without reading its code: module, Go version, features, database, resources with their fields, every route, the environment variables it reads, its marker comments, and `problems` that would stop `goforge add` from working. Use `--json` to read it programmatically.

Each resource serves `GET /<plural>?limit=&offset=`, `POST /<plural>`, `GET /<plural>/{id}`, `PUT /<plural>/{id}`, `PATCH /<plural>/{id}`, and `DELETE /<plural>/{id}`.

## Working in a generated project

- Verify changes with `goforge check --json`: it runs gofmt, go vet, go test, and golangci-lint (if installed), and returns `ok` plus a `problems` list where each problem has a `step` (`format`, `vet`, `test`, or `lint`), `file`, `line`, `message`, and, for tests, the `test` name. Exit status 1 means something failed. A generated project passes it. (`go test ./...` and `make lint` also work.)
- Keep the `// goforge:` marker comments: GoForge edits files only at those markers, so later `goforge add` commands depend on them.
- `.goforge.json` records the project's options, resources, and database. Don't edit it by hand.
- Configuration comes from environment variables: `APP_ENV` (`production` or `development`), `PORT`, `DATABASE_URL`, `LOG_LEVEL`, `LOG_FORMAT`, `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, `MAX_BODY_BYTES`, `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT`.
- Run the server with `make run` while developing: it sets `APP_ENV=development`, so a 500 response includes its cause in `detail`. Error responses from the generated handlers are JSON with a `request_id`; the server's log lines for that request carry the same ID, and unexpected errors are logged with their cause. (Unknown routes and unsupported methods get Go's plain-text 404 and 405, which still carry the `X-Request-ID` header.) Plain `go run .` uses production mode, without `detail`. Log from your own code with `handlers.Logger(ctx)` to include the request ID.
- `GET /health` reports liveness and `GET /readyz` readiness, including the database.
- `GET /openapi.json` serves an OpenAPI 3.1 description of the API: paths, schemas with the field rules, pagination, and errors. It is generated from `.goforge.json` and regenerated by `goforge add resource`: don't edit `openapi/openapi.json`. Use it to learn or call the API, or to generate a client. Projects generated by earlier versions don't have it.
- With Docker databases: `make db-up` starts the database, `make test-db` runs the tests against it.

## MCP server

`goforge mcp` runs an MCP server over stdio. Claude Code: `claude mcp add goforge -- goforge mcp`. Tools: `goforge_generate` (a whole project with resources and database, in one call), `goforge_add_resource`, `goforge_add_db`, `goforge_inspect` and `goforge_check` (both read-only). Each returns the same JSON as the command with `--json`; a failure is a tool error with the `code` and `hint`. Tools take the project directory as an argument.

## Agent skill

`skills/goforge/SKILL.md` teaches an agent when and how to use GoForge. Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add Frank5ive/Goforge`, then `/plugin install goforge@goforge`.
